subject: Request: Align Backup Purge SLA with Subprocessor Deletion Guarantees
messages:
From: Emma Smith <emma.smith@dataclinic.com>
To: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@dataclinic.com
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Backup purge timing + confirmation of subprocessor deletion guarantees

Hi Rafael,

Thanks for taking this on. As part of our DPA review we need to reconcile Dataclinic's 45-day deletion expectation for customer data with Redwood's backup purge cadence and the guarantees your subprocessors provide. Specifically: 

- When a customer requests account deletion via API, what is the maximum time until all related log entries and backups created by Redwood and any subprocessors are purged?
- Do your subprocessors (storage, backups, monitoring) apply the same deletion trigger and can they provide a contractual commitment (or can Redwood provide an SLA amendment) that binds them to that timeline?

We have a strict regulatory window for some patient-identifiable logs and we'd like to include explicit language in the addendum. Procurement is aiming to finish legal review by next Friday, so any firm numbers and a redline would be hugely helpful.

Thanks,
Emma
Emma Smith
Head of Security & Privacy
Dataclinic Health
emma.smith@dataclinic.com

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Smith <emma.smith@dataclinic.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 11:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge timing + confirmation of subprocessor deletion guarantees

Hi Emma — appreciate the clear ask. Looping in Kimberly (privacy), Laura (ops), and Aditya (platform) to get definitive numbers and the subprocessor commitments. Below is what I can commit to now and the items we need to confirm: 

What I can confirm today:
- When a deletion API call is received and processed, Redwood marks the primary customer records for deletion immediately. Primary datastore deletion completes within 24–72 hours depending on queued writes.
- Backups are pruned on a rolling schedule; most short-term snapshots are eligible for purge within 30 days of mark-for-deletion, but longer-term retention windows (for disaster recovery snapshots) can extend that window.

Open items we will confirm by end of day tomorrow: 
1) Exact maximum time until all backup/replica data and monitoring logs are purged across all subprocessors.
2) Whether our major subprocessors will accept contractual language to reduce their purge window to a firm 45 days post-delete request (or an agreed SLA amendment).
3) What evidence we can provide (audit log exports, signed attestation from subprocessor) to include in the addendum.

I'll attach a preliminary subprocessor matrix and a draft SLA amendment for your review — Kimberly, can you drive the language and sign-off? Laura / Aditya, please confirm deletion runbook steps and what we can automate for evidence exports.

Rafael
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: subprocessor-matrix.csv (stub)
Attachment: draft-sla-amendment.docx (stub)

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Smith <emma.smith@dataclinic.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Apr 2026 15:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge timing + confirmation of subprocessor deletion guarantees

Hi Emma — thanks for the summary and Rafael for coordinating. I pulled the details together after syncing with Ops and Procurement. Key points and proposed language below (high-level):

Summary (proposed commitment):
- Redwood will ensure that, for customer-initiated account deletion requests, primary customer data is logically deleted within 72 hours and physical removal from active datastores will be complete within 30 days.
- Short-term backups and snapshots that are not required for regulatory retention will be purged within 45 days of the deletion request.
- For longer-term DR/archival snapshots we will provide a carve-out schedule in the DPA addendum — these will be explicitly enumerated and must be mutually agreed (e.g., snapshots retained for legal/contractual retention).
- Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to bind subprocessors to the same 45-day purge commitment where feasible and will provide either a) a subprocessor attestation or b) an SLA amendment that identifies any subprocessors that cannot meet 45 days with justification.

Proposed DPA addendum phrasing (snippet):
"Upon receipt of a Customer27s deletion request, Redwood Inference will promptly mark all Customer Data for deletion. Except for data subject to preservation obligations or specific retention carve-outs agreed in writing, Redwood will ensure that (i) primary data stores are removed from active production within 30 days, and (ii) backups and snapshots are purged within 45 days. Redwood will use commercially reasonable efforts to obtain equivalent commitments from its subprocessors and will disclose any subprocessor exceptions within thirty (30) days of such request."

Evidence and operational notes: 
- We can provide an audit export showing deletion request timestamps and job run IDs. Aditya: can you confirm we can produce a per-customer audit log (CSV) showing trigger -> job -> snapshot purge events within 7 business days?
- Laura: Ops suggests we add a scheduled purge job to run daily for marked deletions to avoid multi-day batching delays; can you confirm ETA to enable this?

Attachments: I attached a draft SLA addendum and an internal subprocessor matrix indicating which vendors currently support programmatic deletion. Please review and propose redlines.

Kimberly Park
Director, Privacy and Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com

Attachment: draft-sla-amendment.docx (stub)
Attachment: subprocessor-matrix.csv (stub)

From: Emma Smith <emma.smith@dataclinic.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@dataclinic.com
Date: Thu, 2 Apr 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Backup purge timing + confirmation of subprocessor deletion guarantees

Kimberly / Rafael — this is helpful and close to what our privacy team needs. A few quick clarifications before we route to legal: 

1) The proposed "45 days" for backups is acceptable as long as the carve-outs are limited and clearly enumerated. Please include an explicit example of a carve-out in the addendum (e.g., "snapshots retained solely for court-ordered preservation or customer-requested archival exports").
2) We will need at least one form of audit evidence attached to the addendum — ideally a sample CSV export that demonstrates deletion_request_ts, job_id, snapshot_id, and purge_ts. Can you provide a one-off sample for a redline review?
3) If any named subprocessors cannot meet the 45-day purge commitment, we will need a short written justification and a mitigation (e.g., escrowed logs, customer-controlled encryption keys).

Procurement is ready to move once we have the sample export and the redline for the addendum. If you can get those to us by end of day tomorrow, I will circulate to our legal team.

Thanks — Emma

--
Emma Smith
Head of Security & Privacy
Dataclinic Health
emma.smith@dataclinic.com
